method: Cloned 14 repos blobless in the Higgsfield sandbox; for every candidate re-read README and LICENSE at the pinned SHA and at HEAD, git history of LICENSE, of the media file and (pickaxe) of README references; re-ran curl on media_url; re-ffprobed all 18 files; re-checked dates against arXiv abs pages, Hugging Face API createdAt and README news lines; ran a temporal-variance static-overlay scan, OCR (RapidOCR) on sampled frames and Whisper on the Ovi audio. No frame could be viewed.
limitations: No frame of any clip was viewed by anyone; content-level checks (real people, brands, in-scene text) are heuristic only.
Higgsfield video_analysis jobs queued by H5 were still 'queued' when checked.
Genmo blog (primary announcement for Mochi 1) not retrievable; Mochi date rests on HF repo metadata and the initial commit.
api.github.com is rate limited from the sandbox; repository authorship was read through git history and public profile pages.
Not legal advice: no clip is rated 'clear' because none of the repos names its demo media in a licence; all accepted items rest on repo-level licences and are 'clear_with_conditions' at best.
